# SYNTHETIC -- hand-written to the documented `sacct --parsable2` format, NOT
# captured from a real cluster. Replace this file with genuine Klone output:
#
#   SLURM_TIME_FORMAT=%s sacct -j <ids> -X --duplicates --noheader \
#     --parsable2 --format=JobIDRaw,State,Partition,Start,End,ElapsedRaw,AllocTRES
#
# Keep this header when you do; the parser skips lines starting with '#'.
#
# Columns: JobIDRaw|State|Partition|Start|End|ElapsedRaw|AllocTRES
#
# One job ID, three attempts -- this is what `--duplicates` buys you. Without
# that flag sacct returns only the last row and the first two preemptions'
# GPU-hours vanish. The third attempt is still running, so End is empty.
# Elapsed: 1800 + 2700 + 900 = 5400 seconds across the three attempts.
12345700|PREEMPTED|ckpt-all|1758045000|1758046800|1800|billing=80,cpu=8,gres/gpu=2,mem=64G,node=1
12345700|PREEMPTED|ckpt-all|1758047000|1758049700|2700|billing=80,cpu=8,gres/gpu=2,mem=64G,node=1
12345700|RUNNING|ckpt-all|1758050000||900|billing=80,cpu=8,gres/gpu=2,mem=64G,node=1
# A step row. `-X` should already have suppressed these, but sacct's flags
# differ between Slurm versions and a step counted as an attempt would double
# the bill, so the parser drops anything with a '.' in JobIDRaw.
12345700.batch|COMPLETED|ckpt-all|1758045000|1758046800|1800|cpu=8,mem=64G,node=1
# An attempt that was cancelled while still pending: it never started, so it
# has no Start and consumed nothing. The parser skips it.
12345701|CANCELLED by 123456||||0|
